why: formal-fixer was required because startup is a release-blocking cross-device failure with ambiguous ownership. The Zod-validated evidence does not demonstrate a package-owned compatibility defect: on ZTE A2022P, the TapTap host process com.taptap throws a FATAL EXCEPTION on its own LightWorkThread before InstantGameActivity or the Cocos first frame appears; Android then force-finishes TapTap PageProxyActivity and shows a TapTap crash dialog. The exception stack body is absent. OPPO PDBM00 is present only in the backend table without raw logs or or a package SHA, while the supplied OPPO raw branch is PKB110/Android 16 and cannot substitute for PDBM00/Android 9. RED first showed that the project lacked this explicit ownership/device-identity contract. GREEN adds only the structured startup contract; no speculative game workaround, vendor modification or unrelated gameplay change was made. The single Cocos Creator 3.8.8 build with official plugin 1.2.2 produced a fresh auditable ZIP, and 18/18 tests, lint, typecheck and package checks pass. That engineering evidence cannot clear natural/perceptual startup on the two failed devices, so status remains BLOCKED. Context intentionally omitted: other games/runs, web-lite, WeChat/Douyin, shared factory code, unrelated gameplay/assets, unbound performance evidence, unavailable proprietary TapTap source and invented backend rules.
